reviews.rationale: Readiness is decided by any ready_for_candidate_approval flag being exactly True; repair artifact presence without that evidence yields blocked, candidate graph presence yields not_reached. This is an ordered lifecycle rule.
The ready_for_candidate_approval OR, repair-content blocking and candidate-exists branches are already owned by named PredicateSpec rules inside FirstMatch.with_fallback(candidate_approval_state).

Absent approval_intent is interpreted differently depending on approval readiness; active_intent_count > 0 or requested status establishes requested, while blocked status establishes blocked. These are lifecycle decisions.
The absence/readiness, positive active_intent_count/requested and blocked predicates are already named PredicateSpec branches in candidate_approval_intent_state.

An approved decision plus readiness.ready is required for materialized; rejected/needs_context/superseded block, dry_run and failure have ordered outcomes, and execution decision references can establish materialization. These encode lifecycle evidence precedence.
Approved-ready, dry_run, failed, blocked and execution-materialized cases already belong to named PredicateSpec branches of candidate_approval_decision_state.

Execution evidence takes priority unless unavailable/not_reached, then requested promotion takes priority, and materialized approval establishes ready. The selected site owns this ordered promotion lifecycle decision.
Execution precedence, requested state and approval-materialized readiness are already represented by named PredicateSpec branches in platform_promotion_state.
A missing promotion request is unavailable only after materialized approval; ok or promotion_ready establishes requested and positive error_count blocks. This is a lifecycle evidence rule.
The absent-after-approval, requested, blocked and unknown cases are already owned by named PredicateSpec branches of promotion_request_state.

dry_run precedes error_count/failure and blocking; commit_created or review_opened establishes executed. Missing execution depends on requested promotion. These are durable lifecycle evidence decisions.
The dry_run, failed, blocked, executed and unavailable-after-request outcomes already have named PredicateSpec ownership in promotion_execution_state.
review_probe_only with merged is deliberately unknown; canonical open/merged and closed states precede summary fallbacks. This defines what review evidence may establish lifecycle status.
Probe-only merged suppression and canonical/summary review-state precedence already appear as named PredicateSpec rules in review_status.

Probe-only review evidence forces not_reached; absent publication is unavailable only after merged review, and published evidence precedes dry_run/failure/blocking. This is publication lifecycle policy.
Probe suppression, review prerequisite and publication result predicates are already owned by the named read_model_publication_state FirstMatch specification.

A non-ready original pre-SIB report blocks unless materialization_source is repair_loop_preview; that exception turns the condition into a warning. Supporting _pre_sib_original_blocked makes the repair allowance explicit.
pre_sib_ready and the repair_loop_preview exception already determine READY/BLOCKED/REPAIRED_PREVIEW through named PredicateSpec branches of _PRE_SIB_STATE_DECISION.

Requirements receive placeholder acceptance criteria unless they already have nonempty refs and every ref names an existing criterion. This coverage rule drives add_acceptance_criterion actions, beyond the incidental ID formatting.
The nonempty references plus all-existing coverage condition is already owned by acceptance_criterion.already_covered in _ACCEPTANCE_CRITERION_DECISION with ADD_PLACEHOLDER fallback.

A strong claim is downgraded to hypothesis when reliability is at most 2 or unavailable and evidence_refs is empty; stronger reliability or evidence prevents repair. Supporting helpers expose the threshold and strong-claim test.
Invalid/non-strong/supported claim cases and DOWNGRADE fallback are already owned by named PredicateSpec rules in _UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM_DECISION.

The whole function combines preview authority stamping (canonical_mutations_allowed and tracked_artifacts_written False), applied_to_preview filtering and op-specific graph mutation for append/add_acceptance_criterion/replace_claim_type. Behavioral dispatch is visible, but a single Specification opportunity for this mixed selection is unclear.
missing_context: Intended boundary between preview authority invariants, action applicability and operation dispatch.

reviews.rationale: append /edges, add_acceptance_criterion and replace_claim_type already dispatch to distinct behaviors through named PredicateSpec branches in _PREVIEW_OPERATION_DECISION; handlers show graph updates rather than an unowned admissibility rule.

unresolved_count == 0 with resolved_count > 0 means improved; positive resolved_count means partially improved; unresolved ontology/candidate families establish distinct blocked states. This is candidate quality classification policy despite count/result packaging.
All-resolved, some-resolved and each unresolved gap-family predicate already belong to named PredicateSpec branches in candidate_quality_review_state.

Readiness is normalized only when pre-SIB is ready, repair loop is not already ready, there are no findings and both applied_action_count and context_required_count are zero. Those explicit prerequisites authorize clean no-op pass-through.
The pre-SIB-ready, repair-not-ready, no-findings and zero-count conjunction is already owned by CLEAN_PRE_SIB_NOOP_PASSTHROUGH PredicateSpec and its supporting predicate.
The exact selected expression merely counts prepared decision rows whose decision_state equals accepted. It does not decide whether any underlying proposal deserves acceptance.

count_decision_states aggregates already prepared exact state values into three counts; its docstring preserves traversal/KeyError semantics and supporting predicates already own the state comparisons.
isinstance(value, dict) selects a representation or empty-dict fallback. There is no domain eligibility or lifecycle decision.
The selected function strips nonempty strings and otherwise returns a caller-supplied default. This is text normalization.

Allocation must match workspace_identity, source_ref, expected_commit and declaration hash while both allocation and initialization authorization flags are exactly True. The conjunction binds bootstrap authority to the specific requested workspace evidence.
Lowercasing, replacing non-alphanumeric runs, trimming dashes and applying a fallback construct a slug representation.
The function initializes node degrees and increments known endpoints for each from/to edge reference. This is graph aggregation without a domain admissibility outcome.
The function finds the first node whose normalized id equals node_id or returns None. This is data lookup.
Nonempty string checking, Z offset replacement and datetime.fromisoformat with ValueError fallback parse a timestamp representation.
Missing endpoints and negative elapsed values return None; otherwise duration is calculated and rounded. These are arithmetic validity and representation checks.
A nonpositive denominator prevents division and the ratio is rounded to six places. This is numerical computation.

A composite record key built from node/gap/decision-or-request/match/resolution identifiers is used for first-occurrence deduplication. The selected site performs record representation cleanup, without deciding evidence acceptance.
Repeated JSON keys raise ValueError while pairs build an object. This is unambiguous parsing enforcement.
os.open/fstat enforce regular-file input; reading limit + 1 bytes and rejecting oversize data bounds I/O. No product authority or eligibility rule is shown.
sha256(data).hexdigest computes a digest representation; it does not decide trust or evidence admissibility.
Mapping type, unknown-field and required-field set checks enforce generic object shape supplied by callers.
Recursive string-key checks prevent YAML-to-JSON rewriting of trace mappings. This is representation preservation.
asdict conversion, legacy field omission, provenance optional-field preservation and trace_context_json decoding implement exchange serialization.

The selected function checks request/container shape, parses references/topology, canonicalizes YAML and constructs immutable request/change values. It carries expected digests without deciding whether a write is authorized.
The string/type and [0-9a-f]{64} regex checks validate the lowercase complete SHA256 format.

The function combines slash normalization and absolute/parent-traversal rejection with admission by PROMOTION_PATH_PREFIXES. The prefix allowlist could define promotion authority, but its values and ownership are omitted.
missing_context: PROMOTION_PATH_PREFIXES values and the intended promotion authority boundary.

reviews.rationale: String normalization and absolute/parent/current-directory segment rejection are mixed with PROMOTION_PATH_PREFIXES admission. It is unclear whether this is a durable allowed promotion scope or a technical path guard.
missing_context: PROMOTION_PATH_PREFIXES values and callers establishing the authority scope of approval.

reviews.rationale: Approval requires a ready active candidate, canonical_mutations_allowed and tracked_artifacts_written exactly False, active_candidate source mode and specified product workflow/governance/repository roles. These explicit prerequisites define candidate admissibility beyond incidental artifact-format checks.

Claim support requires requested criteria to exist and be bound, required elements to exist, validation_issues to be empty, an exact nonambiguous anchor set, matching source identity and resolved anchors with blob identity. This is a durable evidence acceptance rule; malformed-evidence guards support that decision.

The whole validator mixes exact fields/profile/digest/signature-envelope format checks with digest binding, canonical identity matching and issuer authority matching. Trust policy predicates are present, but no narrow selected decision boundary separates them from signed-format enforcement.
missing_context: Intended Specification boundary between signed decision schema enforcement and authority/evidence binding.

reviews.rationale: Origin requires no existing subject, one revision and one activation; later writes must append exactly one immutable-history revision and preserve containment and disposition. These are explicit lifecycle transition permissions.

An ordered lifecycle decision gives published precedence over open/merged review, requested promotion and materialized/ready approval; later branches infer repaired/rerun/repair/intake stages from artifact presence. The selected site owns this stage precedence.

The selected function decides lifecycle precedence and repaired readiness using candidate nodes, clarification questions and zero unresolved gap counts; medium/high findings and remaining blockers produce blocker identifiers. These are lifecycle and blocker rules.

Recursive dictionary export excludes keys in RAW_TRACE_FIELDS and every raw_ prefix while retaining other string keys. That explicit field-admissibility predicate defines a publication disclosure rule, even though traversal is mechanical.

The exact function chooses the first truthy preferred/fallback artifact. Without callers it could be generic lookup mechanics or authoritative evidence selection; the shown helpers do not resolve which.
missing_context: Callers defining what preferred/fallback artifacts mean and whether selection establishes authoritative evidence.

reviews.rationale: Most of the function calculates phase durations, but it extends the final phase to now when blocked_or_open or last_phase == lifecycle_state. Whether that inclusion test is measurement mechanics or lifecycle measurement policy cannot be established from the shown context.
missing_context: Callers and metric definition for blocked_or_open and ongoing final-phase duration.

reviews.rationale: A handoff preview must exist, be a candidate_spec_graph under the expected contract, have candidate nodes and forbid canonical mutations/tracked writes with exact False. These explicit requirements decide preview admissibility and constrain authority.
